# The Economy of Oathlord
This feature is: [color=red]Heavily In-Progress[/color].
## Currencies
The currency which is used to buy and sell objects in Oathlord is called "Na".
At this moment, there are 3 variations of Na, each having a different value.
- Na: It has a copper form, and a value of 1. Most payments are measured in Na. - Nar: It has a silver form, and a value of 100 Na. - Nara: It has a gold form, and a value of 1000 Na, or 10 Nar.
## Accounts
All players have an account in the economy, where their stored Na can be seen. An account is automatically created once a player spawns with their job.
In order to get access to information regarding your account, you must interact with the Transaction Machine, which holds data about all active accounts in the economy.
## Transaction Machine
The transaction machine is the main machine used to do operations on individual accounts. Those operations can be: - Depositing money on an account. - Withdrawing money from an account. - Adding a loan to an account. - Paying a loan from an account.
You may open the machine's UI by clicking on it, or via right-click -> Toggle UI.
Once it's open, look to the left. As you have noticed, the machine has a Ledger, which automatically shows you all accounts registered in the economy. By clicking on an account, the UI will change to represent information about the current selected account.
Such information can be: - How much money the current account owns - The name of the account owner - The transaction history of said account
The transaction history is an important part in validating transactions. It ensures people who try to do illegal operations are logged and seen.
## Vault/Treasury
There's no physical vault as of now, however the economy stores a specific set of currencies which can be used for transactions. This means you have to be careful when handling transactions, in order to not make the economy go bankrupt.
## Loans
A loan can be requested by a player in order to get temporary Na on their name. Loans have their own separate history on the machine's UI, of which it mentions if the given loans are paid, and when they are due to be paid.
It is up to the player operating the machine to decide if the other player is worthy of getting a loan.
Loans, aside from giving access to Na, also have an interest which is set and managed by the economy. By default, the player will have to re-pay extra 10% interest, however that can change throughout the round.
E.g. Giving a 200 Na loan means the player will have to pay 220 Na to the bank later.
